newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Uganda plans telecoms privatisation forum in April.
newsitem.headline: Uganda plans telecoms privatisation forum in April.

text.p: Uganda, pushing ahead with one of Africa's more aggressive privatisation programmes, plans a forum for investors in the telecommunications sector on April 17, Finance Minister Matthew Rukikaire said on Monday.
The government planned to issue a new national licence to provide competition for Uganda Telecommunciations which the government is selling off, he told a pan-African privatisation conference.
To date, the country has divested itself of 63 of 117 state-owned enterprises. Major sell-offs remained to be completed in several areas.

The government is also looking to privatise sugar producer Kinyara, the national Dairy Corporation and the Coffee Marketing Board, although so far it has not received sufficiently attractive offers for the coffee concern, Rukikaire said.

In the banking sector the government is seeking a buyer for its 51 percent stake in the largest bank, Uganda Commercial Bank, and is also looking divest its minority shareholdings in Barclays Bank and Bank of Baroda, he added.
Other privatisation targets include Uganda Airlines, the National Insurance Corporation, the National Housing Corporation and state-run hotels.
